engineering/planning/OA-ROADMAP-HF-009/15-EXECUTIVE-ARCHITECTURE-SUMMARY.md:3:Status: `PLANNING SUMMARY — PROPOSED, NON-AUTHORITATIVE`
engineering/planning/OA-ROADMAP-HF-009/15-EXECUTIVE-ARCHITECTURE-SUMMARY.md:5:Operational Alpha’s integrated architecture has one simple rule: author an engineering fact once, under one owner, and derive every other representation from its immutable, versioned metadata. HF-005 supplies the lifecycle and gate analysis; HF-006 supplies synchronization and generated-artifact discipline; HF-007 supplies the EMM contract; HF-008 supplies versioning, migration, qualification, and reusable capabilities.
engineering/planning/OA-ROADMAP-HF-009/15-EXECUTIVE-ARCHITECTURE-SUMMARY.md:7:The resulting end-to-end path is authorization → metadata → capability execution → evidence → qualification → acceptance/reconciliation → closeout. Each handoff identifies the owner, source facts, projection boundary, verification mechanism, and lifecycle relation. Generated artifacts and runtime state remain directional projections, and version-aware consumers such as Zeus report incompatibility rather than guessing.
engineering/planning/OA-ROADMAP-HF-009/15-EXECUTIVE-ARCHITECTURE-SUMMARY.md:9:The architecture is ready for implementation planning, not operational adoption. The minimum practical start is a canonical schema/owner vocabulary, manifest-based validation, immutable fact/version storage, and a small deterministic generator. Concrete transports, persistence, interfaces, and adoption decisions remain intentionally open implementation work.

engineering/planning/OA-ROADMAP-HF-008/05-METADATA-MIGRATION-FRAMEWORK.md:1:# Metadata Migration Framework

engineering/planning/OA-ROADMAP-HF-008/05-METADATA-MIGRATION-FRAMEWORK.md:5:A migration transforms a qualified source revision into a successor authoritative revision or a derived compatibility projection. It is directional, repeatable, version-pinned, and auditable.
engineering/planning/OA-ROADMAP-HF-008/05-METADATA-MIGRATION-FRAMEWORK.md:9:| Plan | source/target schemas, scope, owner, compatibility and rollback declared | migration manifest |

engineering/planning/OA-ROADMAP-HF-008/01-ENGINEERING-METADATA-LIFECYCLE.md:3:Status: `PROPOSED LOGICAL CONTRACT — NON-AUTHORITATIVE`
engineering/planning/OA-ROADMAP-HF-008/01-ENGINEERING-METADATA-LIFECYCLE.md:5:An EMM entity revision progresses deterministically through `DRAFT → VALIDATED → QUALIFIED → PUBLISHED → ADOPTED → SUPERSEDED | DEPRECATED → RETIRED → ARCHIVED`. A failed validation or qualification returns the candidate to `DRAFT`; it never changes a published immutable revision. `RETIRED` stops new use, while `ARCHIVED` preserves the immutable record and its lineage.
engineering/planning/OA-ROADMAP-HF-008/01-ENGINEERING-METADATA-LIFECYCLE.md:9:| Create | Identified need and stable identity | candidate fact | declared authoritative owner |

engineering/planning/OA-ROADMAP-HF-008/01-ENGINEERING-METADATA-LIFECYCLE.md:14:| Revise | successor is required | new linked candidate revision | authoritative owner |
engineering/planning/OA-ROADMAP-HF-008/01-ENGINEERING-METADATA-LIFECYCLE.md:15:| Deprecate/retire/archive | replacement or retention policy is met | constrained use, then preserved history | authoritative owner and archive custodian |
engineering/planning/OA-ROADMAP-HF-008/01-ENGINEERING-METADATA-LIFECYCLE.md:17:Publication is not adoption. Adoption is per consumer and is recorded as an immutable compatibility binding. Synchronization can project a published revision only source-to-target; no projection changes the source revision.
